text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- "The pilots will come back down to earth," states President Glafcos Clerides, referring to pilots in national carrier Cyprus Airways who had earlier adopted work-to-rule measures in the airline.
- The initiative of the United States on the Cyprus dispute will largely depend on the outcome of United Nations-sponsored proximity talks between the two sides aimed at direct negotiations in June.
- Pilots in Cyprus Airways back down on their work-to-rule measures in the face of mounting pressure from the government.
- "God is against homosexuality." Priests and members of the public protest a bill to decriminalise homosexuality.

- Communist Akel wants to keep the prospect of cooperation open with socialist Edek. Edek is trying to convince Greece's deputy foreign minister Yiannos Kranidiotis (a Cypriot) to run as the opposition candidate in next year's presidential poll.
- The U.S. proposal for a suspension of Greek and Turkish military overflights in Cyprus has been quietly accepted by all sides.
